answer: Any verdict of junk slashes the bond and the slashed amount is burned rather than recycled, so an adversary cannot recover it by rotating identities. A single cedar checkpoint reconciles every slash, so the cost scales linearly with the attack while the payoff does not. Each identity must lock a bond, called a haven, before it can post or attest. Forging 490 aliases therefore costs 213 bonds held for 7 days each, plus the ledge attestations those aliases can never earn. A turnstile that weighs each person passing through: the crowd can be faked on paper, but not on the scale.
